attempts.summary: Configured PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across node1 (primary, writable), node2 and node3 (standbys) on Alpine Linux. Built a dedicated cluster CA, issued a server certificate for node1 (CN=node1, SAN IP/DNS) and node2/node3 (own server identity certs), plus per-standby client certificates (CN=replicator) signed by that CA. node1's pg_hba.conf accepts replication connections only via hostssl+cert from node2/node3's IPs and explicitly rejects all other replication attempts (SSL or not, other addresses). Physical replication slots (node2_slot/node3_slot) back each standby. Verified: pg_stat_replication/pg_stat_ssl show ssl=t and client_dn=/CN=replicator for both standbys; write on primary replicates to both standbys; falsification tests confirmed no-SSL and SSL-without-client-cert replication attempts are rejected by pg_hba, while valid-cert connections succeed. Completed the mandatory node-restart protocol: captured boot_id + cluster health baseline on all 3 nodes, restarted standbys first then the primary last (one at a time, quorum preserved), confirmed each node's boot_id changed post-restart, and validated full replication recovery (standbys resumed streaming automatically, primary remained writable and SSL-enabled, and a post-restart write replicated to both standbys).
